_what_this_is: User-agent tokens for crawlers that feed AI systems: model training,
retrieval-augmented answers, and the live fetches an agent makes on a
user's behalf. `robots.ai-crawler-blocked` reports when a site's
Hand-curated. Each entry cites the operator's own published documentation,
because a user-agent token nobody can check against its source is folklore
and this list decides what we tell an operator about their own site.
_this_is_not_a_defect: Blocking AI crawlers is a legitimate, and increasingly common, decision.
The finding is a Warning and its wording must never read as though the site
It exists because the decision is usually *inherited* rather than made:
WordPress security and SEO plugins add these blocks by default, and the
site owner often does not know. Making an unexamined default visible is
the whole value. Confirming it and moving on is a perfectly good outcome.
_purpose_matters: `purpose` separates two very different things, and a report that conflates
`training` — the crawler collects text to train a model. Blocking it has no
effect on whether an assistant can answer questions about the site today.
`retrieval` — the crawler fetches pages to answer a user's question, now,
often because that user asked about this site. Blocking it means the site
is invisible at the moment somebody is actively looking for it, which is
usually not what the operator intended.
`both` — the operator uses one token for both, or does not distinguish.
_absent_deliberately: Search-engine crawlers — Googlebot, Bingbot — are out of scope here. A site
blocking Googlebot has a much larger problem than this check describes, and
conflating 'not in AI answers' with 'not in search results' would bury the
more serious finding inside the newer one.
Scrapers with no published documentation are also absent. Without a source
to cite, an entry is a rumour.

note: Not a crawler with its own user agent. It is a token Googlebot honours
to decide whether already-fetched content may be used for Gemini and
AI Overviews. Blocking it does NOT affect Search indexing, and the
finding must say so or it reads as a far more serious problem.
